### US-047 — Submit Support Ticket
*Epic: EPIC-011  |  Role: Customer  |  Related requirement(s): FR-047*

**Story:** As a Customer, I want to submit a support ticket describing my issue, optionally linked to a specific Booking, so that I can do so quickly, reliably, and with confidence the result is correct.
**Business value:** The system shall allow a Customer or Provider to submit a support ticket describing their issue, optionally linked to a specific Booking.
**Preconditions:** Customer is authenticated and has the permissions required for this action
**Trigger:** Customer initiates the 'Submit Support Ticket' action

**Main flow:**
  1. Customer opens the create/add action to submit a support ticket describing their issue, optionally linked to a specific Booking
  2. Customer fills in the required fields
  3. System validates each required field as it is entered and again on submit
  4. System saves the new record (as Draft or Pending where the module defines that status)
  5. System confirms creation and displays the newly created record

**Alternative flow:** None
**Exception flow:** System displays a clear, specific error message and preserves the user's input for correction

**Data validation:**

| Field | Field type | Mandatory / Optional | Validation rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Name / title | Text | Mandatory | Cannot be blank; trimmed; 2-100 characters; unsupported characters rejected |
| Email | Email | Mandatory | Valid email format; must be unique — checked before the record is saved |
| Description | Text | Optional | Up to 1,000 characters; may be left empty |
| Attachment | File upload | Optional | Allowed formats and size limit enforced before upload |

**Error messages:**
- A required field is blank -> "Please complete this required field."
- A value already exists -> "This value is already in use. Please choose another."
- The save fails on the server -> "We couldn't save your changes. Please try again."

**Empty states:**
- No records exist yet -> "Nothing here yet." with a primary call-to-action to add the first one

**Edge cases:**
- User double-clicks Submit -> only one record is created (duplicate submissions are ignored)
- Session expires while the form is open -> user signs in again and the entered data is preserved
- Network drops during save -> the user sees a retry option and no partial record is stored

**Business rules:**
- Every support ticket must be linked to the requesting user's account and, where relevant, the associated Booking.
- A ticket may not be closed without a recorded resolution note.
- A ticket that references a Booking must be visible to the agent alongside that Booking's current status and history.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Given customer submits the form with all required fields valid, when they confirm, then a new record is created and is immediately visible to customer.
- Given invalid or incomplete input, when customer attempts to submit a support ticket describing their issue, optionally linked to a specific Booking, then the system rejects the action with a specific, actionable error message.
- Given customer lacks the permissions required for this action, when they attempt to submit a support ticket describing their issue, optionally linked to a specific Booking, then the system denies the action and does not reveal data beyond what customer is authorized to see.
- Given there is no data to show, when customer opens this area, then the system displays the defined empty-state message with a clear next action.
- Given an edge case such as a duplicate submission or an expired session, when customer attempts to submit a support ticket describing their issue, optionally linked to a specific Booking, then the system behaves as defined in the edge cases and never leaves partial data.

**Story:** As an Admin, I want to escalate a ticket to a senior agent or Admin when it cannot be resolved at the first level, preserving the full ticket history, so that I can do so quickly, reliably, and with confidence the result is correct.
**Business value:** The system shall allow a Support agent to escalate a ticket to a senior agent or Admin when it cannot be resolved at the first level, preserving the full ticket history.
**Preconditions:** Admin is authenticated and has the permissions required for this action
**Trigger:** Admin initiates the 'Escalate Ticket' action

**Main flow:**
  1. Admin opens the queue of items awaiting a decision
  2. Admin reviews the relevant details before deciding whether to escalate a ticket to a senior agent or Admin when it cannot be resolved at the first level, preserving the full ticket history
  3. Admin confirms the decision, optionally with a reason/note
  4. System applies the decision, updates the record's status, and records the action in the audit log
  5. System notifies the affected user(s) of the outcome

**Alternative flow:** Admin saves as draft and returns later, where applicable
**Exception flow:** System rejects the decision if the record's state has since changed (e.g. already actioned by another Admin), and does not apply a partial update

**Data validation:**

| Field | Field type | Mandatory / Optional | Validation rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Decision | Selection | Mandatory | One of approve / reject / suspend / override |
| Reason / note | Text | Mandatory | Required for reject, suspend and override; 10-500 characters |
| Record state | System check | Mandatory | Decision accepted only while the record is still pending |

**Error messages:**

- Reason left blank on a reject/suspend -> "Please enter a reason for this decision."

- Target user or record was deleted meanwhile -> the action is cancelled with an explanatory message

- Given an edge case such as a duplicate submission or an expired session, when admin attempts to escalate a ticket to a senior agent or Admin when it cannot be resolved at the first level, preserving the full ticket history, then the system behaves as defined in the edge cases and never leaves partial data.

**Story:** As an Admin, I want to make use of "Operational Dashboard", so that I can do so quickly, reliably, and with confidence the result is correct.
**Business value:** The system shall present an at-a-glance operational dashboard (active Bookings, exceptions, recent activity) for Admin/Operations.
**Preconditions:** Admin is authenticated and has the permissions required for this action
**Trigger:** Admin initiates the 'Operational Dashboard' action

**Main flow:**
  1. Admin opens the relevant list/search screen
  2. Admin enters a query or applies filters/sort to make use of "Operational Dashboard"
  3. System returns matching results, updating as the query or filters change
  4. System shows a clear empty state with guidance if no results match

**Alternative flow:** None
**Exception flow:** System displays a clear, specific error message and preserves the user's input for correction

**Data validation:**

| Field | Field type | Mandatory / Optional | Validation rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Search text | Text | Optional | Trimmed; maximum 100 characters; special characters handled safely; empty shows the default list |
| Filters | Selection | Optional | Values must come from the available options |
| Sort order | Selection | Optional | Limited to the supported sort options; a default applies if none is chosen |
| Page / page size | Number | Optional | Positive whole numbers within the supported range |

**Error messages:**
- The search service is unavailable -> "We couldn't load results. Please try again."
- An invalid filter combination is requested -> "Those filters can't be combined. Reset filters to continue."

**Empty states:**
- No results match -> "No results match your search or filters." with a Reset filters button and suggestions

**Edge cases:**
- Very long or empty query -> empty query shows the default list; over-long input is truncated with a notice
- Filters that would return zero results are disabled or hidden to avoid dead ends

**Business rules:**
- Financial reports must reconcile to the underlying payment records — no report may show a different total than the sum of its source transactions.
- A report or export must only include data the requesting role is authorized to see (e.g. Support sees ticket data, not full financial detail).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Given no records match the current query or filters, when results are returned, then the system shows an explicit empty state rather than a blank screen.
- Given invalid or incomplete input, when admin attempts to make use of "Operational Dashboard", then the system rejects the action with a specific, actionable error message.
- Given admin lacks the permissions required for this action, when they attempt to make use of "Operational Dashboard", then the system denies the action and does not reveal data beyond what admin is authorized to see.
- Given there is no data to show, when admin opens this area, then the system displays the defined empty-state message with a clear next action.
- Given an edge case such as a duplicate submission or an expired session, when admin attempts to make use of "Operational Dashboard", then the system behaves as defined in the edge cases and never leaves partial data.

### US-064 — Security Audit Logging
*Epic: EPIC-014  |  Role: Admin  |  Related requirement(s): FR-064*

**Story:** As an Admin, I want to make use of "Security Audit Logging", so that I can do so quickly, reliably, and with confidence the result is correct.
**Business value:** The system shall log authentication events and authorization failures for later security review.
**Preconditions:** Admin is authenticated and has the permissions required for this action
**Trigger:** Admin initiates the 'Security Audit Logging' action

**Main flow:**
  1. Admin opens the queue of items awaiting a decision
  2. Admin reviews the relevant details before deciding whether to make use of "Security Audit Logging"
  3. Admin confirms the decision, optionally with a reason/note
  4. System applies the decision, updates the record's status, and records the action in the audit log
  5. System notifies the affected user(s) of the outcome

**Alternative flow:** Admin saves as draft and returns later, where applicable
**Exception flow:** System rejects the decision if the record's state has since changed (e.g. already actioned by another Admin), and does not apply a partial update

**Data validation:**

| Field | Field type | Mandatory / Optional | Validation rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Decision | Selection | Mandatory | One of approve / reject / suspend / override |
| Reason / note | Text | Mandatory | Required for reject, suspend and override; 10-500 characters |
| Record state | System check | Mandatory | Decision accepted only while the record is still pending |

**Error messages:**
- Record already actioned by another admin -> "This item has already been processed."
- Reason left blank on a reject/suspend -> "Please enter a reason for this decision."

**Empty states:**
- The review queue is empty -> "Nothing is waiting for review." with a link back to the dashboard

**Edge cases:**
- Two admins act on the same item simultaneously -> the first decision wins and the second sees a conflict message
- Target user or record was deleted meanwhile -> the action is cancelled with an explanatory message

**Business rules:**
- Every state-changing action must check the acting user's role/permission before executing, not only hide the option in the UI.
- Sensitive data (payment details, identity documents) must be encrypted at rest and only decrypted for authorized processing.
- A security audit log entry must never itself contain the raw sensitive data (e.g. full card numbers, passwords) involved in the event it records.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Given the action is destructive or high-impact, when admin confirms it, then the system records admin, a timestamp, and the stated reason in the audit log before applying it.
- Given invalid or incomplete input, when admin attempts to make use of "Security Audit Logging", then the system rejects the action with a specific, actionable error message.
- Given admin lacks the permissions required for this action, when they attempt to make use of "Security Audit Logging", then the system denies the action and does not reveal data beyond what admin is authorized to see.
- Given there is no data to show, when admin opens this area, then the system displays the defined empty-state message with a clear next action.
- Given an edge case such as a duplicate submission or an expired session, when admin attempts to make use of "Security Audit Logging", then the system behaves as defined in the edge cases and never leaves partial data.

### US-070 — Data Export / Right to Access
*Epic: EPIC-016  |  Role: Customer  |  Related requirement(s): FR-070*

**Story:** As a Customer, I want to request and receive a machine-readable export of the personal data the platform holds about me, so that I can do so quickly, reliably, and with confidence the result is correct.
**Business value:** The system shall allow a user to request and receive a machine-readable export of the personal data the platform holds about them.
**Preconditions:** Customer is authenticated and has the permissions required for this action
**Trigger:** Customer initiates the 'Data Export / Right to Access' action

**Main flow:**
  1. Customer navigates to the relevant screen
  2. Customer provides the information required to request and receive a machine-readable export of the personal data the platform holds about them
  3. System validates the input
  4. System completes the action and confirms the result

**Alternative flow:** Customer saves as draft and returns later, where applicable
**Exception flow:** System displays a clear, specific error message and preserves the user's input for correction

**Data validation:**

| Field | Field type | Mandatory / Optional | Validation rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Required input(s) | Text | Mandatory | Must be present and in a valid format before the action is processed |
| Optional input(s) | Text | Optional | May be left empty; validated only when provided |
| Record state | System check | Mandatory | Action allowed only when the record is in a state that permits it |

**Error messages:**
- Required input is missing or invalid -> "Please check the highlighted fields and try again."
- The action isn't permitted in the current state -> "This action isn't available right now."
- A connected service times out -> "This is taking longer than expected. Please try again."

**Empty states:**
- No related data exists yet -> "Nothing to show yet." with guidance on how to get started

**Edge cases:**
- The action is triggered twice in quick succession -> it is processed once (idempotent)
- A dependent service times out mid-action -> no partial result is stored and the user can retry safely

**Business rules:**
- A user-initiated account deletion request must be honored within the platform's published retention/deletion window; data required for legal/financial record-keeping may be retained only as long as that obligation requires, clearly separate from the rest of the deleted account.
- A user may withdraw consent for any optional (non-essential) data use at any time, without needing to delete their entire account.
- Withdrawing optional consent or requesting deletion must never be harder to do than the original opt-in/signup action.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Given customer meets the preconditions, when they request and receive a machine-readable export of the personal data the platform holds about them with valid input, then the system completes the action and confirms it clearly.
- Given invalid or incomplete input, when customer attempts to request and receive a machine-readable export of the personal data the platform holds about them, then the system rejects the action with a specific, actionable error message.
- Given customer lacks the permissions required for this action, when they attempt to request and receive a machine-readable export of the personal data the platform holds about them, then the system denies the action and does not reveal data beyond what customer is authorized to see.
- Given there is no data to show, when customer opens this area, then the system displays the defined empty-state message with a clear next action.
- Given an edge case such as a duplicate submission or an expired session, when customer attempts to request and receive a machine-readable export of the personal data the platform holds about them, then the system behaves as defined in the edge cases and never leaves partial data.

*Epic: EPIC-016  |  Role: Customer  |  Related requirement(s): FR-071*

| Field | Field type | Mandatory / Optional | Validation rule |
|---|---|---|---|

| Current password | Password | Mandatory | Required only for security-affecting changes (password, email); re-authentication enforced |

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Given invalid or incomplete input, when customer attempts to make use of "Consent Management", then the system rejects the action with a specific, actionable error message.
- Given customer lacks the permissions required for this action, when they attempt to make use of "Consent Management", then the system denies the action and does not reveal data beyond what customer is authorized to see.
- Given an edge case such as a duplicate submission or an expired session, when customer attempts to make use of "Consent Management", then the system behaves as defined in the edge cases and never leaves partial data.

artefacts.content_markdown:
# Product Requirements Document (PRD)

**Project:** An app where people book home cleaners and pay online
**Generated:** 2026-10-07

## 1. Product Overview
An app where people book home cleaners and pay online. This product addresses the problems identified in the Business Requirements Document by giving Individual consumers a structured, end-to-end digital workflow in place of manual coordination.

**Competitive positioning:** For individual consumers who need a better way to complete a booking, this booking platform product offers a structured, transparent alternative to manual and generic options. A specific differentiator has NOT yet been stated and must be defined.

**Key differentiators:**
- Structured, end-to-end workflow — Weak defensibility

**Main alternatives:** Established platforms and apps in the booking platform space (Direct); General-purpose marketplaces, classifieds and social groups (Indirect); Manual and offline alternatives (Substitute)

*Feasibility verdict: **GO WITH CHANGES**. See the Feasibility & Competitive Assessment document for the full analysis.*

## 2. Product Goals
- Validate the core booking workflow with early Individual consumers
- Reduce the manual operational work required to run the business
- Increase transparency for customers and providers throughout a booking
- Reach initial operational and financial viability for the MVP scope

## 3. Target Users & Personas
**Target users:** Individual consumers

- **Primary Customer** (Individual consumers) — Find and complete a Booking for the right Service with minimal friction
- **Active Provider** (Provider offering Services on the platform) — Get discovered, win Bookings, and get paid reliably
- **Operations / Admin User** (Internal team member responsible for day-to-day platform operation) — Keep the platform running smoothly and resolve exceptions quickly

## 4. User Journeys
- Customer Journey: Customer discovers the platform, searches for a service, reviews options, completes a booking, and leaves a review after completion.
- Provider Journey: Provider applies to join, is verified, publishes services, manages incoming bookings, and gets paid.
- Admin/Operations Journey: Admin monitors the exception queue, moderates flagged services, resolves disputes, and reviews operational reports.
- Support Journey: Support agent receives a ticket, reviews the linked account/transaction context, resolves or escalates, and closes with a resolution note.

## 5. Product Capabilities
- Authentication & Account Management
- User Profile Management
- Search & Discovery
- Service Catalog
- Booking & Checkout
- Scheduling & Availability
- Payments & Billing
- Provider Management
- Reviews & Ratings
- Notifications
- Customer Support & Help
- Admin & Operations Console
- Reporting & Analytics
- Security & Access Control
- Onboarding & Activation
- Privacy, Consent & Data Retention

## 6. Functional Requirements
### FR-001 — Customer/Provider Registration
- **Purpose:** The system shall allow a new Customer or Provider to create an account using a supported identifier (email or phone) and password, or a supported third-party identity provider. Required fields, format validation, and duplicate-account prevention must be enforced before the account is created.
- **Actor:** Customer
- **Trigger:** Customer initiates the 'Customer/Provider Registration' action
- **Preconditions:** Customer does not already have an account
- **Inputs:** Customer fills in the required fields
- **Expected behavior:** System performs: Customer/Provider Registration. The system shall allow a new Customer or Provider to create an account using a supported identifier (email or phone) and password, or a supported third-party identity provider. Required fields, format validation, and duplicate-account prevention must be enforced before the account is created.
- **Outputs:** Confirmation of the completed action, Updated record state
- **User-visible result:** User sees a clear success confirmation and, where applicable, the updated record
- **Validation:** Enforces: A Customer or Provider must verify their identifier (email or phone) before completing a Booking.; Accounts are uniquely identified by email or phone; duplicate accounts for the same identifier are not permitted.
- **Error scenarios:** System displays a clear, specific error message and preserves the user's input for correction, Permission denied for the acting role, Required field missing or fails format validation
- **Dependencies:** N/A

## 7. Roles & Permissions
- **Customer:** Search/browse, create Bookings, manage own profile, submit reviews, raise support tickets.
- **Provider:** Create/edit own Services, manage own availability, view own Bookings and payouts.
- **Support Agent:** View relevant Booking/account context for a ticket; respond to and close tickets.
- **Admin:** Full read access; manual overrides with recorded reason; access to reporting and audit logs.

## 8. Product Business Rules
- BR-001: A Customer or Provider must verify their identifier (email or phone) before completing a Booking.
- BR-002: Accounts are uniquely identified by email or phone; duplicate accounts for the same identifier are not permitted.
- BR-003: After 5 consecutive failed login attempts, the account is temporarily locked for a cooldown period.
- BR-004: A Customer or Provider may only view and edit their own profile, except where an Admin role is explicitly granted override access.
- BR-005: Changing the primary contact identifier (email/phone) requires re-verification.
- BR-006: A user's display name must be unique enough to avoid confusion in shared views (e.g. booking history, reviews) but is not required to be globally unique.
- BR-007: Only active, published Services are returned in search and browse results.
- BR-008: Filters must be combinable (e.g. category AND price range AND location) rather than mutually exclusive.
- BR-009: Search relevance ranking must not be purchasable/manipulable by a Provider outside of clearly labeled promoted placements, if any exist.
- BR-010: A Service must have a title, description, price, and at least one category before it can be published.
- BR-011: A Provider may only edit or remove their own Services; Admins may moderate any listing.
- BR-012: An Service that is out of stock or unavailable must not be bookable/purchasable until restocked or re-enabled.
- BR-013: A Booking may only be created against an Service that is currently published and available.
- BR-014: The total cost shown to the Customer before confirmation must match the amount actually charged.
- BR-015: A Booking moves through a defined status lifecycle (pending, confirmed, in progress, completed, cancelled) and may not skip states.
- BR-016: A Provider may not have two confirmed Bookings that overlap in time.
- BR-017: A slot is held for the Customer for a limited window during checkout; if payment is not completed in that window, the slot is released.
- BR-018: Raw payment card details must never be stored directly by the platform; only a processor-issued token/reference is retained.
- BR-019: A refund may not exceed the original captured amount for that Booking.
- BR-020: A Booking is not considered confirmed until payment capture succeeds.
- BR-021: Only an approved, active Provider may publish Services or accept Bookings.
- BR-022: A Provider whose rating or cancellation rate falls below the platform's minimum threshold is flagged for review.
- BR-023: A Customer may only review a Booking they actually completed, and only once per Booking.
- BR-024: A Provider may publicly respond to a review but may not delete a review outright; disputed reviews go through Admin moderation.
- BR-025: A user may opt out of non-essential notification categories, but not out of security- and Booking-critical notifications (e.g. payment confirmation).
- BR-026: Notifications must be sent within a short, bounded delay of the triggering event to remain useful.
- BR-027: Every support ticket must be linked to the requesting user's account and, where relevant, the associated Booking.
- BR-028: A ticket may not be closed without a recorded resolution note.
- BR-029: A ticket that references a Booking must be visible to the agent alongside that Booking's current status and history.
- BR-030: Every manual override performed by Admin/Operations must be recorded with the acting user, timestamp, and reason.
- BR-031: Destructive actions (e.g. removing a Provider, cancelling a Booking) require explicit confirmation before executing.
- BR-032: Admin/Operations views must never expose raw payment credentials, even to resolve a support case.
- BR-033: Financial reports must reconcile to the underlying payment records — no report may show a different total than the sum of its source transactions.
- BR-034: A report or export must only include data the requesting role is authorized to see (e.g. Support sees ticket data, not full financial detail).
- BR-035: Every state-changing action must check the acting user's role/permission before executing, not only hide the option in the UI.
- BR-036: Sensitive data (payment details, identity documents) must be encrypted at rest and only decrypted for authorized processing.
- BR-037: A security audit log entry must never itself contain the raw sensitive data (e.g. full card numbers, passwords) involved in the event it records.
- BR-038: Onboarding must be skippable/dismissible and must never block access to the core product.
- BR-039: An account's onboarding state must persist across sessions and devices.
- BR-040: A user-initiated account deletion request must be honored within the platform's published retention/deletion window; data required for legal/financial record-keeping may be retained only as long as that obligation requires, clearly separate from the rest of the deleted account.
- BR-041: A user may withdraw consent for any optional (non-essential) data use at any time, without needing to delete their entire account.
- BR-042: Withdrawing optional consent or requesting deletion must never be harder to do than the original opt-in/signup action.

## 9. Navigation Pattern
Top navigation bar (desktop and mobile)

A single top navigation bar surfaces the core booking platform workflow first (Authentication & Account Management, User Profile Management, Search & Discovery, Service Catalog); secondary items (settings, account, support) are accessible from it but not primary.

## 10. Notifications & Confirmations
- Account created — delivered via Email + In-app
- Email/phone verification — delivered via Email + In-app
- Password reset requested — delivered via Email + In-app
- Password changed — delivered via Email + In-app
- Suspicious login detected — delivered via Email + In-app
- Profile updated — delivered via In-app + Push
- Contact identifier changed — delivered via In-app + Push
- Listing published — delivered via In-app + Push
- Listing out of stock — delivered via In-app + Push
- Listing flagged/moderated — delivered via In-app + Push
- Booking created — delivered via In-app + Push
- Booking confirmed — delivered via In-app + Push

## 11. Validation & Error Handling
All forms validate required fields client-side before submission; server-side validation errors are surfaced with actionable, field-specific messages. Every functional requirement above defines its own error scenarios explicitly rather than relying on a single generic error state.

## 12. State Behaviors
- **Loading:** Show a loading indicator while an action is processing
- **Empty:** Show a clear empty state with a call to action when no data exists yet
- **Success:** Show explicit confirmation of the completed action
- **Failure:** Show a clear error message with a retry or correction path
- **Processing:** Disable the triggering action while in progress to prevent duplicate submissions

## 13. Audit & Versioning
Admin/Operations actions are recorded in an append-only audit log (see BRD Section 16.6). Full version history of records is not required for the MVP scope.

## 14. Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR-001 [Performance] The system shall respond to standard user-facing actions within 2 seconds under normal load.
- NFR-002 [Performance] Search and listing pages shall return results within 1.5 seconds for catalogs up to 100,000 items.
- NFR-003 [Scalability] The system shall support horizontal scaling of stateless application components as transaction volume grows.
- NFR-004 [Scalability] The data layer shall support at least 10x current expected launch volume without architectural rework.
- NFR-005 [Availability] Core user-facing functionality shall target 99.5% monthly uptime post-launch.
- NFR-006 [Reliability] A failed payment or network error shall never leave a transaction in an ambiguous or double-charged state.
- NFR-007 [Security] All traffic between client and server shall be encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher.
- NFR-008 [Security] The system shall enforce role-based access control on every state-changing server endpoint.
- NFR-009 [Privacy] Personally identifiable information shall be encrypted at rest and access-logged.
- NFR-010 [Accessibility] All primary user flows shall meet WCAG 2.2 AA where applicable.
- NFR-011 [Usability] First-time users shall be able to complete the core workflow without external instructions.
- NFR-012 [Maintainability] The codebase shall follow a documented architecture and coding standard to support ongoing maintenance.
- NFR-013 [Compatibility] The system shall support the latest two major versions of common desktop and mobile browsers.
- NFR-014 [Monitoring] The system shall emit structured logs and metrics sufficient to diagnose production incidents.
- NFR-015 [Logging] Security-relevant events (login, permission denial, payment) shall be logged with actor, timestamp, and outcome.
- NFR-016 [Backup] Production data shall be backed up on a regular, automated schedule with tested restore procedures.
- NFR-017 [Disaster Recovery] A documented recovery plan shall define target recovery time and recovery point objectives.
- NFR-018 [Localization] Text content shall be externalized to support future localization, even if only one language ships at launch.

### Expected scale and usage

Planning for up to 500 registered users in the first 12 months (peak up to 50 concurrent, designed for 100) with a 99.0% during business hours availability target.

| Parameter | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Registered users — first 12 months | Under 500 | Stated |
| Registered users — planning horizon (36 months) | about 2,000 (4x the 12-month figure) | Assumed — confirm |
| Peak concurrent users (first 12 months) | Under 50 | Stated |
| Design capacity (2x peak headroom) | 100 concurrent users | Derived |
| Sustained request rate at design capacity | about 20 requests/second (assuming about one request every 5 seconds per active user) | Derived |
| Availability target | 99.0% during business hours (allowed downtime: about 7 hours per month (outside business hours: best effort)) | Stated |
| Recovery time objective (RTO) / recovery point objective (RPO) | 8 hours / 24 hours | Stated |
| Launch geography | One city or region | Stated |
| Sensitive data handled | Personal details (names, emails, phone numbers) | Stated |
| Client platforms | Web application | Stated |

*Status: **Stated** = taken from your discovery answers; **Assumed — confirm** = a planning default because the question was not answered; **Derived** = calculated from those volumes; **Proposed — confirm** = good-practice requirement that needs your confirmation. Nothing marked Assumed or Proposed is a confirmed fact.*

### Availability and recovery

- **Availability target:** 99.0% during business hours (allowed downtime: about 7 hours per month (outside business hours: best effort))
- **Recovery time objective (RTO):** 8 hours
- **Recovery point objective (RPO):** 24 hours
- **Basis:** Stated

### Performance requirements

| ID | Metric | Target | Condition | How it is measured | Priority | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PERF-001 | Page / screen load time (95th percentile) | 2.0 seconds or better; Largest Contentful Paint 2.5 seconds or better | on a typical broadband or 4G connection, at up to 100 concurrent users | Real-user monitoring and synthetic tests | P0 | Derived from stated volumes |
| PERF-002 | API response time — reads (95th / 99th percentile) | 300 ms / 800 ms | at up to 100 concurrent users | APM percentile dashboards; load test | P0 | Derived from stated volumes |
| PERF-003 | API response time — writes (95th percentile) | 500 ms | at up to 100 concurrent users | APM percentile dashboards; load test | P0 | Derived from stated volumes |
| PERF-004 | Error rate | below 0.5% of requests | at up to 100 concurrent users | APM error-rate alert; load test | P0 | Derived from stated volumes |
| PERF-005 | Sustained throughput | at least 20 requests per second with targets above still met | steady load for 30 minutes | Load test | P0 | Derived from stated volumes |
| PERF-006 | Background jobs and notifications | delivered within 60 seconds of the triggering event (95th percentile) | normal load | Queue-latency metric | P1 | Derived from stated volumes |
| PERF-007 | Payment step (excluding provider time) | 3 seconds or better | normal load | APM trace of the checkout flow | P0 | Derived from stated volumes |

### Scalability requirements

| ID | Requirement | Target | Approach | How it is verified | Priority | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SCL-001 | Horizontal scaling of the application tier | Scale out automatically to hold the performance targets up to 100 concurrent users | Stateless instances behind a load balancer; autoscaling on CPU (target 60%) and request latency, with a minimum of 2 instances | Load test with a ramp to the design capacity | P0 | Derived from stated volumes |
| SCL-002 | Capacity headroom | Handle 2x the expected peak (50 -> 100 concurrent users) with no degradation of the performance targets | Capacity model reviewed before launch and after each doubling of users | Load test at 2x peak plus a spike test at 3x | P0 | Derived from stated volumes |
| SCL-003 | User growth | Support growth from about 500 to about 2,000 registered users (36-month planning horizon) without re-architecture | Database read replicas, connection pooling, caching of read-heavy data, and a documented partitioning/archiving plan before tables exceed ~50 million rows | Architecture review at each 2x growth; load test on synthetic data at 36-month volume | P1 | Derived from stated volumes |
| SCL-004 | Data growth | Storage, indexes and backups shall grow with data without slowing the main flows | Indexing standards, archive of old records, lifecycle rules on object storage | Query-plan review; storage-growth dashboard | P1 | Derived from stated volumes |
| SCL-005 | Graceful degradation under overload | When capacity is exceeded, non-critical features (recommendations, analytics, exports) shall be shed first so core flows keep working | Feature flags, queue-based processing for spikes (notifications, reports), request shedding with clear user messaging | Chaos/overload test | P1 | Derived from stated volumes |
| SCL-006 | Load testing | A repeatable load-test suite shall exist and run before launch and before each major release | Scenarios for the main user journeys at expected, peak and 2x-peak volumes | Reports archived per release | P0 | Derived from stated volumes |

## 15. Technical & Integration Constraints
- **Application type:** Recommended: responsive web application; TBD: native mobile app for a later phase
- **Major system capabilities:** Authentication & Account Management; User Profile Management; Search & Discovery; Service Catalog; Booking & Checkout; Scheduling & Availability; Payments & Billing; Provider Management; Reviews & Ratings; Notifications; Customer Support & Help; Admin & Operations Console; Reporting & Analytics; Security & Access Control; Onboarding & Activation; Privacy, Consent & Data Retention
- **External integrations:** Payment Gateway; Email Delivery; SMS / OTP Provider; Maps / Geolocation; Analytics
- **Data sources:** Account records; Profile records; SearchQuery records; Service records; Booking records; AvailabilityWindow records
- **Api dependencies:** Payment Gateway API; Email Delivery API; SMS / OTP Provider API; Maps / Geolocation API
- **Real time requirements:** Slot-holding during checkout requires near-real-time availability checks; otherwise standard request/response is sufficient.
- **Authentication dependencies:** Recommended: managed authentication provider rather than custom-built auth
- **Platform deployment constraints:** POC/MVP scope — single environment and region initially, not yet designed for multi-region deployment
- **Per-capability technical notes:**
  - **Payments & Billing:** Payments & Billing: payment capture/refunds are delegated to a tokenizing, PCI-compliant processor; the platform never stores raw card data and only holds a processor-issued reference.
  - **Scheduling & Availability:** Scheduling & Availability: slot computation and a short-lived hold during checkout must be handled with a concurrency-safe check to prevent two confirmations of the same slot.

### System requirements

| ID | Category | Requirement | Priority | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SYS-001 | Platform & clients | The product shall be delivered as a responsive web application backed by a versioned HTTPS API that a mobile client can reuse later. | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SYS-002 | Browser & device support | The web client shall support the latest two major versions of Chrome, Safari, Edge and Firefox, on desktop, tablet and phone screen sizes. | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SYS-003 | Hosting & infrastructure | The product shall run on a managed cloud platform with automated instance replacement; a single availability zone is acceptable at this availability target. | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SYS-004 | Architecture | The application tier shall be stateless and horizontally scalable behind a load balancer; session state shall live in a shared store, never on an application server. | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SYS-005 | Data storage | A managed relational database shall be the system of record; object storage shall be used for any generated or uploaded files. | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SYS-006 | Environments & delivery | Separate development, staging and production environments shall exist, provisioned as code, with a CI/CD pipeline that runs automated tests and supports rollback within minutes. | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SYS-007 | Backup & disaster recovery | Automated database backups with point-in-time recovery shall be kept, meeting an RPO of 24 hours and an RTO of 8 hours; a restore shall be tested at least quarterly. | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SYS-008 | Monitoring & observability | Application performance monitoring, centralised structured logs, uptime checks and alerting on the availability and latency targets in this document shall be in place before launch. | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SYS-009 | Integrations | Every third-party integration (email/SMS, payments, analytics) shall be called through an adapter with timeouts, retries with back-off and a circuit breaker, so a provider outage degrades one feature instead of the whole product. | P1 | Proposed — confirm |
| SYS-010 | Configuration & secrets | Environment configuration shall be external to the code, and secrets shall be held in a managed secrets store, never in the repository or client bundles. | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SYS-011 | Time & localisation | All timestamps shall be stored in UTC and displayed in the user's time zone; text shall be stored as UTF-8 to allow later localisation. | P1 | Proposed — confirm |

## 16. Security, Privacy & Access Constraints
- **Authentication requirements:** All core workflow actions require an authenticated session (see FR-001/FR-002 in the Functional Requirements above)
- **Mfa requirements:** Not required for MVP — Recommended for Admin roles in a later phase
- **Roles:** Customer; Provider; Support Agent; Admin
- **Access restrictions:** Customer: Cannot view or edit other users' data; cannot access Admin tooling.; Provider: Cannot view other Providers' data; cannot moderate Services or access Admin tooling.; Support Agent: Cannot perform destructive admin overrides without escalation.; Admin: All actions are logged; destructive actions require explicit confirmation.
- **Sensitive data handling:** Payment data must never be stored directly — delegated to a PCI-compliant processor (see BRD Section 16.5)
- **Privacy requirements:** Applicable privacy and regulatory requirements must be confirmed for the launch geography. In the interim, personal data should be minimized, encrypted at rest, and access-logged, with deletion honored on request.
- **Audit requirements:** Admin/Operations actions are logged; see BRD Section 16.6
- **Approval requirements:** None identified from discovery
- **Ux implications:** Admin-only actions (e.g. approve/reject, moderation, overrides) must not be shown to non-Admin roles; Payment entry screens must clearly indicate secure handling
- **Per-capability security notes:**
  - **Authentication & Account Management:** Authentication & Account Management: passwords/OTPs are hashed/never logged in plaintext; sessions expire on idle timeout and are invalidated on password change.
  - **User Profile Management:** User Profile Management: a user may only view/edit their own profile; changing the primary contact identifier requires re-verification.
  - **Payments & Billing:** Payments & Billing: raw payment credentials are never stored by the platform; only a processor token/reference is retained, and refunds cannot exceed the original captured amount.
  - **Admin & Operations Console:** Admin & Operations Console: every manual override is recorded with actor, timestamp, and reason in an append-only audit log; destructive actions require explicit confirmation.
  - **Privacy, Consent & Data Retention:** Privacy, Consent & Data Retention: account deletion and data-export requests are authenticated before acting on them; deleted data is removed or irreversibly anonymized within the published retention window.

### Security requirements

| ID | Category | Requirement | How it is verified | Priority | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SEC-001 | Authentication | Passwords shall be stored using a modern adaptive hash (Argon2id or bcrypt), be checked against known-breached passwords, and be at least 10 characters; login shall be rate-limited with temporary lockout after repeated failures. | Security review and automated test of the login flow | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SEC-002 | Authentication | Multi-factor authentication shall be available to all users and mandatory for administrators and any user role that can access other people's data or payouts. | Configuration review; admin login test | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SEC-003 | Session management | Sessions shall use short-lived tokens with rotation, secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookies (web), server-side invalidation on logout and password change, and an idle timeout. | Penetration test | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SEC-004 | Authorization | Access shall be enforced on the server for every request using role-based permissions, with object-level checks so one user can never read or change another user's records by changing an ID. | Automated authorization tests per role; penetration test | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SEC-005 | Encryption in transit | All traffic shall use TLS 1.2 or higher with HSTS; plain HTTP shall redirect and internal service-to-service traffic shall also be encrypted. | TLS scan (e.g. SSL Labs grade A) | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SEC-006 | Encryption at rest | Databases, backups and object storage shall be encrypted with AES-256; keys shall be managed in a key-management service and rotated at least annually. | Cloud configuration audit | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SEC-007 | Application security | The product shall be protected against the OWASP Top 10: parameterised queries only, output encoding, CSRF protection, a strict Content-Security-Policy and standard security headers. | SAST/DAST in CI; penetration test | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SEC-008 | Abuse protection | Public endpoints shall have rate limiting and bot/abuse protection (sign-up, login, password reset, search and any messaging or review submission). | Load/abuse test | P1 | Proposed — confirm |
| SEC-009 | Audit logging | Security-relevant events (logins, permission changes, admin actions, data exports, deletions) shall be logged with user, time and origin, protected from modification, and retained for at least 12 months; logs shall not contain passwords, tokens or full payment details. | Log review | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SEC-010 | Vulnerability management | Dependencies shall be scanned on every build, critical vulnerabilities patched within 7 days and high within 30 days, and an independent penetration test performed before launch and at least annually. | CI report; pen-test report | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SEC-011 | Privacy & compliance | Applicable data-protection law for the launch geography (for example GDPR, UK GDPR, CCPA or the India DPDP Act) shall be identified before build; the product shall record consent where required and support access, correction, export and deletion of a person's data. | Legal review; test of the data-request flows | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SEC-012 | Data retention | Each data category shall have a documented retention period, and expired or deleted personal data shall be removed from the live system and from backups within a defined window. | Retention policy review | P1 | Proposed — confirm |
| SEC-013 | Incident response | A written incident-response plan shall define roles, escalation, evidence handling and breach notification to users and regulators within the legally required time. | Tabletop exercise before launch | P1 | Proposed — confirm |
| SEC-014 | Administrative access | Production access shall be limited to named staff on a least-privilege basis, require MFA, and be logged; no shared accounts. | Access review each quarter | P0 | Proposed — confirm |
| SEC-015 | Third-party risk | Every vendor that processes user data shall be assessed and covered by a data-processing agreement before integration. | Vendor register review | P1 | Proposed — confirm |
| SEC-016 | Payment security | Card data shall never touch or be stored on the product's servers: payments shall use a PCI DSS-compliant hosted payment provider, webhooks shall be signature-verified, and payment actions shall be idempotent to prevent double charges. | Provider attestation; payment-flow test | P0 | Proposed — confirm |

## 17. AI Feature Specifications
*This product has no AI-powered features per the business idea and discovery answers.*

## 18. MVP / Phase 2 / Future Scope

### MVP Scope

- FR-011 — Keyword Search

### Phase 2 Scope

### Future Scope

### Out of Scope

## 19. Success Metrics
- Conversion rate
- Completion rate
- Customer satisfaction
- Retention
- Revenue
- Processing time
- Error rate
- Support resolution time

## 20. Dependencies
- Payment Gateway
- Email Delivery
- SMS / OTP Provider
- Maps / Geolocation

- Legal/compliance review prior to launch

## 21. Assumptions
- ASSUMPTION: Individual consumers have internet-connected devices.
- ASSUMPTION: Initial launch targets a single geography.
- ASSUMPTION: A payment processor will be available and integrated for MVP.
- **Confirmed with the stakeholder before drafting:** Is payment taken at booking, after service, or both — At time of booking.
- **Confirmed with the stakeholder before drafting:** Where will your users be located at launch — One city or region.
- **Recommended by AI — please confirm:** What is your decision on: Data retention after account deletion — Delete personal data 30 days after account deletion; keep financial and legal records for the period the law requires. *Why: Gives users a short grace period to change their mind, while transaction records must be kept for tax and dispute purposes.*
- **Recommended by AI — please confirm:** What is your decision on: Platform fee / commission — 10–15% commission on completed bookings, charged to the provider. *Why: A common range for two-sided marketplaces; it only earns revenue when a booking is completed.*

## 22. Release Plan
- **Phase 0 — Discovery**: Finalize requirements, policies, and architecture decisions.
- **Phase 1 — MVP**: Deliver the P0/P1 functionality needed for a usable booking platform product.
- **Phase 1.1 — Stabilization**: Bug fixes, usability refinements, accessibility and performance hardening.
- **Phase 2 — Expansion**: P2/P3 functionality and the future enhancements listed in this document.

artefacts.title: UX Product Flow Specification — An app where people book home cleaners and pay online
artefacts.content_markdown:
# UX / Product Flow Specification

**Project:** An app where people book home cleaners and pay online
**Generated:** 2026-10-07

*This is the primary document intended for the external Design AI Agent. It describes what each screen must contain and how it must behave — not visual designs.*

## 1. Application Information Architecture
- Sign Up / Log In
- Dashboard / Home
- User Profile Management
- Search & Discovery
- Service Catalog
- Booking & Checkout
- Scheduling & Availability
- Payments & Billing
- Provider Management
- Reviews & Ratings
- Customer Support & Help
- Admin & Operations Console
- Reporting & Analytics
- Onboarding & Activation
- Privacy, Consent & Data Retention
- Account Settings

## 2. Screen Inventory
### SCR-001 — Sign Up / Log In
- **Purpose:** Authenticate the user or create a new account
- **Primary role:** Customer
- **Entry points:** First visit, Logged-out state
- **Exit points:** Dashboard
- **Related stories:** US-001, US-002
- **Related requirements:** FR-001, FR-002
- **Primary actions:** Sign up, Log in
- **Secondary actions:** Forgot password
- **Navigation:** Entry point before any authenticated screen
- **Information displayed:** Sign-up/login form
- **Data required:** Email/identifier, Password
- **UI elements required:** Text input, Password input, Submit button
- **Permissions:** Public — no authentication required
- **Business rules:** Requires a valid, unique identifier
- **Dependencies:** N/A

### SCR-002 — Dashboard / Home
- **Purpose:** Primary landing screen after authentication, orienting the user to their next action
- **Primary role:** Customer
- **Entry points:** Post sign-up/login
- **Exit points:** SCR-003, SCR-004, SCR-005
- **Related stories:** US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004, US-005
- **Related requirements:** FR-001, FR-002, FR-003, FR-004, FR-005
- **Primary actions:** Navigate to core workflow

### FLOW-001 — Flow: Customer/Provider Registration
- **Actor:** Customer
- **Goal:** The system shall allow a new Customer or Provider to create an account using a supported identifier (email or phone) and password, or a supported third-party identity provider. Required fields, format validation, and duplicate-account prevention must be enforced before the account is created.
- **Starting point:** Dashboard
- **Preconditions:** Customer does not already have an account
- **Main path:**
    1. Customer opens the create/add action to create an account using a supported identifier (email or phone) and password, or a supported third-party identity provider (SCR-001)
    2. Customer fills in the required fields
    3. System validates each required field as it is entered and again on submit
    4. System saves the new record (as Draft or Pending where the module defines that status)
    5. System confirms creation and displays the newly created record
- **Alternative paths:** None
- **Error paths:** System displays a clear, specific error message and preserves the user's input for correction
- **Decision points:** None
- **Completion state:** Action completed and confirmed to the user
- **Related screens:** SCR-002, SCR-001
- **Related requirements:** FR-001
- **Related stories:** US-001

## 5. Interactions
- **Customer/Provider Registration** — precondition: Acting user has the permissions required for Customer/Provider Registration; behavior: The system shall allow a new Customer or Provider to create an account using a supported identifier (email or phone) and password, or a supported third-party identity provider. Required fields, format validation, and duplicate-account prevention must be enforced before the account is created.; result: Clear confirmation of the completed action; next state: Success state, or the next step in the related flow; possible errors: Validation error, Permission denied, Server error
- **Login** — precondition: Acting user has the permissions required for Login; behavior: The system shall allow a registered user to authenticate using their identifier and password (or one-time code), establishing a session that persists across page reloads until logout or expiry.; result: Clear confirmation of the completed action; next state: Success state, or the next step in the related flow; possible errors: Validation error, Permission denied, Server error
- **View & Edit Profile** — precondition: Acting user has the permissions required for View & Edit Profile; behavior: The system shall allow an authenticated user to view and edit their own profile fields (name, contact details, preferences), with changes validated and saved immediately.; result: Clear confirmation of the completed action; next state: Success state, or the next step in the related flow; possible errors: Validation error, Permission denied, Server error
- **Manage Addresses** — precondition: Acting user has the permissions required for Manage Addresses; behavior: The system shall allow a Customer to add, edit, and remove one or more saved addresses, and to designate a default address used to pre-fill future Bookings.; result: Clear confirmation of the completed action; next state: Success state, or the next step in the related flow; possible errors: Validation error, Permission denied, Server error
- **Keyword Search** — precondition: Acting user has the permissions required for Keyword Search; behavior: The system shall allow a Customer to search the Service Catalog by free-text keyword, matching against Service titles and descriptions, and return ranked results.; result: Clear confirmation of the completed action; next state: Success state, or the next step in the related flow; possible errors: Validation error, Permission denied, Server error
- **Filter Results** — precondition: Acting user has the permissions required for Filter Results; behavior: The system shall allow a Customer to narrow search or browse results using category, price range, and (where applicable) location and availability filters, with the result count updating as filters are applied.; result: Clear confirmation of the completed action; next state: Success state, or the next step in the related flow; possible errors: Validation error, Permission denied, Server error
- **Create Service Listing** — precondition: Acting user has the permissions required for Create Service Listing; behavior: The system shall allow a Provider to create a new Service listing with title, description, price, category, and media, saving it as a draft until required fields are complete.; result: Clear confirmation of the completed action; next state: Success state, or the next step in the related flow; possible errors: Validation error, Permission denied, Server error
- **Edit Service Listing** — precondition: Acting user has the permissions required for Edit Service Listing; behavior: The system shall allow a Provider to edit an existing Service listing's details, with changes reflected to Customers immediately upon save.; result: Clear confirmation of the completed action; next state: Success state, or the next step in the related flow; possible errors: Validation error, Permission denied, Server error
- **Create Booking** — precondition: Acting user has the permissions required for Create Booking; behavior: The system shall allow a Customer to initiate a Booking for a selected Service, capturing all details required (date/time, quantity, address, etc.) before proceeding to payment.; result: Clear confirmation of the completed action; next state: Success state, or the next step in the related flow; possible errors: Validation error, Permission denied, Server error
- **Review Before Confirming** — precondition: Acting user has the permissions required for Review Before Confirming; behavior: The system shall present a review step summarizing the Service, chosen details, and total cost, requiring explicit Customer confirmation before payment is captured.; result: Clear confirmation of the completed action; next state: Success state, or the next step in the related flow; possible errors: Validation error, Permission denied, Server error

## 7. Navigation
- **Pattern:** Top navigation bar (desktop and mobile)
- **Structure:** Exposes Dashboard plus one entry per core module (Authentication & Account Management, User Profile Management, Search & Discovery, Service Catalog, Booking & Checkout), with account settings and support reachable from the same top navigation bar.
- **Mobile behavior:** The same top navigation bar adapts responsively on mobile, collapsing secondary items into an overflow/'More' entry rather than switching to a different navigation structure.

## 8. Notifications & Feedback
- **Success:** Toast/banner confirming the action, auto-dismissing after a few seconds
- **Error:** Inline field-level errors plus a summary banner for form-level failures
- **Loading:** Skeleton or spinner in place of content; primary actions disabled while in flight
- **Empty:** Illustration or message plus a clear primary call to action

## 9. Roles & Permissions Matrix
- **Customer:** View own data, Update own profile, Create/edit own records, Cancel/withdraw own in-progress records
- **Provider:** View own data, Update own profile, Create/edit own records, Cancel/withdraw own in-progress records
- **Support Agent:** View records relevant to an open ticket, Respond to and close tickets
- **Admin:** View all records, Manual override (with recorded reason), Moderate/approve/reject flagged content, Access reporting and audit logs

## 10. Responsive Requirements
- **Desktop:** Full multi-column layouts; primary navigation always visible
- **Tablet:** Collapsible navigation; core flows remain single-column where content is form-heavy
- **Mobile:** Single-column layouts; bottom tab navigation; touch targets at least 44x44px

## 11. Accessibility
- Target WCAG 2.2 AA across primary user flows unless the business context specifies another standard.
- All interactive elements must be reachable and operable via keyboard.
- Form fields must have accessible labels and clear, non-color-only error indication.
